business: Mitra, a Bengaluru app that matches local businesses with Kannada and English creators and counts the customers each post brings
target: Owner-run local businesses in Bengaluru (cafés, restaurants, bakeries, salons, gyms, clinics, boutiques) with 1-3 outlets that spend some money on marketing and have tried or considered Instagram creators
where: Bengaluru (Indiranagar, Koramangala, HSR, Jayanagar, Malleshwaram, Whitefield)

segments.name: Single-outlet café, bakery or restaurant owner, marketing budget ₹5,000-25,000 a month
Salon, gym, clinic or studio owner, books appointments, budget ₹5,000-30,000 a month
2-3 outlet brand or boutique with a marketing person, budget ₹30,000-1,50,000 a month

behaviours.name: Barter only
behaviours.how: Gives creators a free meal or service for a post; has never paid a creator cash.

behaviours.name: Pays creators directly
behaviours.how: Finds creators on Instagram, DMs them, pays ₹2,000-15,000 by UPI, judges by views.

behaviours.name: Uses an agency
behaviours.how: Pays a local digital agency a monthly retainer that includes some influencer posts.

behaviours.name: Boosts posts and runs Zomato/Swiggy ads
behaviours.how: Spends on Meta boosts or aggregator ads; skeptical of influencers.

behaviours.name: Burned by fake influencers
behaviours.how: Paid a creator whose followers turned out fake or who brought no customers.

behaviours.name: Word-of-mouth only
behaviours.how: Relies on Google reviews and regulars; spends almost nothing on marketing.

objections: Influencer posts get views but don't bring paying customers through the door
Most influencers have fake followers; how do I know these are real?
I can just DM creators myself, why pay a middleman?
Barter works fine for me; why pay cash plus a fee?
I don't have time to manage another app or count customers at the till
A 10% fee plus GST on top adds up when margins are thin
Kannada creators might not reach my English-speaking customers (or the reverse)
New app, no track record in my area
habits: you check your Google reviews and Instagram every evening after closing
you've been approached by three 'influencer agencies' this year
you pay suppliers and staff by UPI
creators walk in and offer a reel for a free meal at least once a month
your weekends are busy and weekdays slow
you ask customers 'how did you hear about us' only sometimes
